name: CHEWY INC
parent: PetSmart, Inc. (itself controlled by funds advised by BC Partners)
acquired_date: 2017 (PetSmart acquisition of Chewy); PetSmart control confirmed as of 2020-03-26 and ended 2021-02-12
notes: Grant years FY2020 and FY2021. Chewy's 10-K for fiscal 2019 says that as of March 26, 2020 'PetSmart beneficially owned more than 50% of our outstanding shares of common stock and, together with its affiliates, exercised control over more than 95% of the voting power', and that Chewy is a 'controlled company' under NYSE rules. That covers all of FY2020 (July 2019-June 2020). For FY2021, Chewy's next 10-K says PetSmart held the shares until February 12, 2021, when they were distributed to affiliates of BC Partners, which then controlled a majority of the voting power; so the first seven months of FY2021 were under PetSmart and the rest under the BC Partners funds. PetSmart's own careers site names Phoenix as its home office. The 5000+ band is safe either way: Chewy alone reported about 12,000 employees at February 2, 2020, and it consolidated into PetSmart. Effect on the record: the parent moves from Chewy (FL) to PetSmart (AZ); the size band does not change and neither does the Ohio column. FY2020 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1766502/000176650221000008/chwy-20210131.htm

name: ROGERS INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTS INC
notes: Grant years FY2019 and FY2021, $899,641, the largest unresolved amount in this batch. No owner found and no source to cite. The company's old domain, rogersindustrial.com, has been a parked for-sale listing since at least 2017 and is now offered by HugeDomains, the wayback captures of it are empty frames, and no other working site, release or fetchable news story turned up; Google News RSS returned nothing for the name on every attempt in this session. What evidence there is argues against a parent rather than for one: the Form 5500 for EIN 34-0897539 is filed by Rogers Industrial Products Inc itself, under its own name in Ohio, with 27 participants in 2015, 39 in 2019 and 71 in 2023, which is the pattern of a small company running its own plan rather than a payee folded into a parent's plan. An earlier research pass on this project reached the same dead end. The record stands, but on absence of evidence, not on evidence.

name: MCKESSON CORPORATION
notes: Grant years FY2021 and FY2023. McKesson Corporation is itself the public registrant and files its own 10-K with no parent; the Form 5500 sponsor 'MCKESSON CORPORATION - DELAWARE' is the same company under its state of incorporation, not a different owner. The 10-K for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2023 carries its headquarters in Irving, Texas, the state the record already has.

name: WALGREEN CO
notes: Grant year FY2020 (July 2019-June 2020); Walgreens Boots Alliance became the holding company for Walgreen Co. on December 31, 2014, five years before the grant year, so the parent was in place throughout. Exhibit 21 to the Walgreens Boots Alliance 10-K filed in 2020 lists 'Walgreen Co. Illinois' among its subsidiaries. Both the payee and the parent are in Deerfield, Illinois, and both are 5000+, so nothing in the Ohio or size columns moves; only the parent name is wrong. I did not fetch a document for the December 31, 2014 reorganization date.

name: CLINTON COUNTY PORT AUTHORITY
notes: Grant year FY2020. A county port authority is a political subdivision created by the county under Ohio Revised Code Chapter 4582; it has no owner and no ownership chain, so the question does not apply and the record stands. Graded D because every port authority site I tried returned no readable text, so there is no URL behind this, only the entity type and the government address on Schedule I.

name: SOUTHERN OHIO PORT AUTHORITY
notes: Grant years FY2023 and FY2024. The Southern Ohio Port Authority is a political subdivision, a port authority serving the Portsmouth and Scioto County area, with no owner and no ownership chain. Its own site responded, which is the only reason this is graded above D.

name: CHARTER MANUFACTURING COMPANY INC
notes: Grant years FY2018 and FY2023. Charter Manufacturing's own site says 'We are a privately held family of market leading metals manufacturing businesses' and names its own subsidiaries (Charter Steel, Charter Wire, Charter Casting, Niles Iron and Metal), so it is the top of its chain, not a subsidiary. It is in Mequon, Wisconsin, the state in the record.

name: THE SMEAD MANUFACTURING COMPANY
notes: Grant years FY2022 and FY2023. Smead was family owned in Hastings, Minnesota through both grant years and was sold to TOPS Products of Illinois in June 2025, two years after the later grant year ended. The source is thin: headlines dated June 10 and 11, 2025 in the Google News RSS feed for 'Smead acquisition' from the Star Tribune ('Family-owned Smead Manufacturing, a mainstay in Hastings, sold to Illinois company'), the Pioneer Press and the Minneapolis/St. Paul Business Journal. I could not fetch the article bodies or a company release. The direction is what matters for this pass: the sale is after the grant years, so the record stands.

name: SIERRA NEVADA CORPORATION
notes: Grant years FY2023 and FY2024. The Form 5500 sponsor difference that flagged this row is a renaming, not a parent: Sierra Nevada Corporation renamed itself Sierra Nevada Company, LLC, and both names sit on EIN 88-0094415. The company is owned by its founders rather than by another company, but sncorp.com returned no readable text on any path I tried and Google News RSS was unavailable, so I have no URL to cite and the grade is D. Nothing in the input signals points to an owner: there is no EDGAR registrant and JobsOhio's own report names the company itself.

name: MULTI-COLOR CORPORATION
notes: Grant years FY2016 and FY2019 (the later one ended June 30, 2019). Multi-Color's own Form 8-K says that on July 1, 2019 it completed its merger with a subsidiary of LABL, Inc., an affiliate of Platinum Equity, and became a wholly owned subsidiary of that parent. July 1, 2019 is one day after the FY2019 grant year closed, so during both grant years Multi-Color Corporation was an independent public company and its own ultimate parent. The 8-K cover gives its address as 4053 Clough Woods Dr., Batavia, Ohio, so the current record's parent_hq_state of IL is wrong for the grant period and should read OH. That direction moves $500,000 into the Ohio column, against the project's headline, and it should be checked by someone else before it is applied.

name: R & L Carriers Inc
notes: Grant year FY2018. R+L Carriers' own site presents it as a privately held family trucking business based in Wilmington, Ohio, with no parent named; its Form 5500 is filed under its own name in Ohio. The about pages on the site 404 for an automated fetch, so this rests on the homepage, hence grade C.

name: EDU EVERYTHING INC
notes: Grant year FY2020, $500,000. This payee is a 501(c)(3), which Schedule I itself records, so it has no owners at all. The IRS exempt organizations master file, read through ProPublica's nonprofit API for EIN 45-5145307, lists it as Edueverything Inc of Caledonia, Ohio, exempt since April 2013, with affiliation code 3, the code the IRS uses for an independent organization that is not part of a national or regional grouping, and revenue of about $518,000. So there is no parent and the record stands. Its size is worth a separate look given the dollar amount: a charity with roughly half a million dollars of annual revenue received a $500,000 economic development grant.

name: REPUBLIC STEEL INC
parent: Grupo Simec, S.A.B. de C.V. (through SimRep Co.)
notes: Grant year FY2022 (July 2021-June 2022); acquisition July 2005, sixteen years earlier, so the parent was in place for the whole grant year. Grupo Simec's Form 20-F for 2021 states that in July 2005 Simec and Industrias CH acquired 100% of Republic's capital stock, that 'SimRep, Co. owns 100% of Republic Steel, Inc.', and that Republic's plants include the steel-making and hot-rolling facility in Lorain, Ohio, which is the city on the Schedule I row. Grupo Simec is headquartered at Calzada Lazaro Cardenas 601, Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico, and reports 5,331 employees as of December 31, 2021 (4,448 at the end of 2020, which would be 500-4999; either band is above 500, so the size class is large on both). Industrias CH, S.A.B. de C.V., also of Mexico, is Simec's controlling shareholder with about 82.5% of the series B shares, so the top of the chain is Mexican either way. This moves $500,000 out of the Ohio column.

name: UNITED AIRLINES INC
notes: Grant year FY2024 (July 2023-June 2024). Exhibit 21 to the 10-K for 2023, listing subsidiaries as of February 29, 2024 and so inside the grant year, shows United Airlines, Inc. as a wholly owned subsidiary of United Airlines Holdings, Inc. The holding company structure dates from the 2010 United-Continental merger, long before the grant; I did not fetch a document for that date. Both are headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, and both are 5000+, so only the parent name is wrong.

name: CEMLEB PROPERTIES
notes: Grant year FY2024, $457,564. Cemleb Properties, LTD. at 11315 Ellerman Rd, Minster, Ohio took a JobsOhio Spec Development OSIP grant of $462,000 in January 2022 with zero jobs created or retained and a $986,000 investment, which is the pattern of a local developer putting up a speculative building. No owner found: no company site answered, no other Schedule I row shares the address, no Form 5500 and no EDGAR record exist for the EIN, and Google News RSS was unavailable in this session. Unresolved rather than independent because a spec building is usually built for somebody, and that somebody was not identified.

name: The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company
notes: Grant year FY2018. The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company is itself the public registrant, files its own 10-K with no parent, and is headquartered in Akron, Ohio. The 10-K cited was filed February 8, 2018, inside the grant year.

name: INTEVA PRODUCTS LLC
notes: Grant year FY2020 (July 2019-June 2020); Inteva was formed in 2008 as a Renco acquisition, twelve years earlier. An SEC filing states the relationship directly: ArvinMeritor's Form 8-K of August 4, 2010 describes the buyer of its Body Systems business as 'an affiliate of Inteva Products, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of The Renco Group, Inc., a New York company' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1113256/000120677410001795/arvinmeritor_8k.htm). For the grant year itself, Renco's own fact sheet, archived February 18, 2020, lists Inteva Products among its portfolio companies with 'Year Acquired: 2008', describes Renco as 'Private, family-owned', and reports 'Over 12,000 portfolio company employees worldwide'. Renco is at One Rockefeller Plaza, New York. The record moves from Inteva itself (MI, 500-4999) to Renco (NY, 5000+); the size class stays large and no Ohio dollars are involved. Graded B rather than A because the grant-year confirmation is a company website, not a filing.

name: OWENS STATE COMMUNITY COLLEGE

name: 4440 CREEK ROAD PROPERTIES LLC
notes: Grant year FY2019, $350,000. I could not establish a formal ownership chain, but the operating company behind this single-purpose LLC is identifiable and should be recorded. The Schedule I address is 4440 Creek Road, Cincinnati 45242, and Graphic Village's own contact page gives 'Cincinnati headquarters 4440 Creek Road Cincinnati, Ohio 45242' (https://www.graphicvillage.com/contact). JobsOhio also paid GRAPHIC VILLAGE LLC $600,000 in FY2021 at that same address, which appears on the Schedule I row for that year. The usual arrangement is that the owners of the business hold the building in a separate LLC, which makes this a sibling of Graphic Village rather than its subsidiary, so I am not calling it owned. Graphic Village is an Ohio company, so nothing moves in the Ohio column either way; the value of this is for the site-development classification, where the row currently rests on a name rule and no operating company.

name: City of Toronto
notes: Grant years FY2017 and FY2018. The City of Toronto, Ohio is a municipal corporation with no owner, so the question does not apply. Graded D because the city's site did not respond to an automated fetch.

JobsOhio's monthly reports name it as Resonant Sciences LLC in 2021, 2023 and 2026.

name: AK STEEL CORPORATION
acquired_date: 1994 (holding company structure); Cleveland-Cliffs bought the holding company 2020-03-13, after the grant year

Second, the Form 5500 sponsor for this EIN now reads Cleveland-Cliffs Steel Corporation, which is the renaming of this same entity after Cleveland-Cliffs bought AK Steel; that merger closed March 13, 2020, nine months after the grant year ended, so it does not apply to this row. name: MCWANE INC
notes: Grant years FY2023 and FY2024. McWane, Inc.'s own site refers to the 'fifth generation of family-owned company' in naming its president, with no outside parent. It is headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, the state in the record.

name: Wilbert Plastic Services
acquired_date: no acquisition before the grant; Alleghany Capital bought a 45% minority interest on 2017-08-01, after the grant year
notes: Grant year FY2017 (July 2016-June 2017). The Form 5500 sponsor on this EIN is WILBERT, INC. of North Carolina, which is the legal entity behind the Wilbert Plastic Services trade name rather than an outside owner, so the sponsor mismatch here is a name, not a parent. The nearest thing to an owner is Alleghany Corporation: its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2017 says 'On August 1, 2017, Alleghany Capital acquired a 45 percent equity interest in Wilbert', a minority stake accounted for under the equity method, in Wilbert Funeral Services, Inc. of Overland Park, Kansas. That is one month after the grant year closed and it is not control, so the record stands. Wilbert Plastic Services' own site gives its corporate headquarters as Huntersville, North Carolina (https://www.wilbertplastics.com/about), matching the state in the record, and the 5500 reported 1,701 participants in 2015, consistent with the 500-4999 band. Berkshire Hathaway later bought Alleghany, in 2022, which is well after this grant.

name: Pretzel Baron Properties LLC
acquired_date: after 2017-09 and before 2023 (exact date not found)
notes: Grant year FY2018 (July 2017-June 2018). This is the row the Form 5500 signal flagged hardest, because the plan sponsor on this exact EIN now reads DITSCH USA LLC, and Ditsch is a brand of Valora of Switzerland, which FEMSA of Mexico bought in 2022. The timing does not support a correction. Pretzel Baron's own website, captured September 3, 2017 and so inside the grant year, describes the company as a family business: 'Pretzel Baron is a new extension of the Servatii Family', the Gottenbusch family's Cincinnati bakery business. JobsOhio's own monthly report for October 2017 also names the company as Pretzel Baron LLC. The Ditsch name appears on this EIN only in the 2023 Form 5500 and in JobsOhio's January 2024 monthly report, which lists a separate later grant to Ditsch USA, LLC. So there is a foreign parent now but not during FY2018, and the record stands with $200,000 in the Ohio column. The weak point is that I could not find the acquisition date itself: no Valora or Ditsch release, SEC filing or fetchable news story gave it, and Valora's site publishes only recent releases. The conclusion rests on the payee's own site describing family ownership during the grant year.

name: EXCELITAS TECHNOLOGIES CORP
acquired_date: not applicable (private-equity owned since 2010, no corporate parent)
notes: Grant year FY2020. A PerkinElmer press release filed with the SEC on December 3, 2010 says PerkinElmer 'completed the sale of its Illumination and Detection Solutions (IDS) business to Excelitas Technologies Corp., an affiliate of Veritas Capital Fund Management, L.L.C., a New York-based private equity firm' and gives Waltham, Massachusetts as the base of that business. Excelitas has been held by private-equity owners since, AEA Investors from 2017, so there is no operating corporate parent whose headquarters or size would displace the payee's, which is how this project has handled other private-equity holdings. Grade C rather than higher because the document is from 2010 and I could not fetch anything covering the grant year itself: excelitas.com returns no readable text to an automated fetch, Google News RSS was unavailable in this session, and the only current EDGAR hits are credit funds holding Excelitas debt, which shows it is privately held but does not name an owner. The record's Massachusetts headquarters and 500-4999 band stand.

name: WILSON SPORTING GOODS COMPANY
parent: Amer Sports, Inc. (ANTA Sports Products Limited is its largest shareholder)
acquired_date: 1989 (Amer acquired Wilson); subsidiary confirmed as of 2023-12-31
notes: Grant year FY2024 (July 2023-June 2024). Amer Sports' Form 20-F for 2023, filed March 2024 and covering the first half of the grant year, describes Wilson Sporting Goods as one of its brands, lists Wilson Sporting Goods Co. among its consolidated subsidiaries, and reports more than 11,400 employees across 41 countries as of December 31, 2023. Amer Sports, Inc. is incorporated in the Cayman Islands but states that 'our corporate offices are located at Konepajankuja 6, 00511 Helsinki, Finland', so Finland is the headquarters. ANTA Sports, which has its principal place of business in China, is the largest shareholder; a strict ultimate-parent reading would put the top of the chain in China. The ownership long predates the grant: Amer has owned Wilson since 1989, a date I could not source from a document I fetched, but the 20-F establishes ownership inside the grant year, which is what the question turns on. The record moves from Wilson itself (IL) to Amer Sports (Finland); the size band does not change and no Ohio dollars are involved.

name: CHARTER NEXT GENERATION INC
acquired_date: not applicable (private-equity owned, no corporate parent)
notes: Grant year FY2023. Charter Next Generation is a private-equity holding, not a subsidiary of an operating company: Leonard Green & Partners co-investment vehicles filed Form D notices in June 2021 that reference the company (for example https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1822584/000182258421000001/primary_doc.xml), and its own site names no parent. Under the convention this project has used for private-equity holdings the operating company keeps its own state and size band, so the record stands on ownership. One separate flag, outside this pass: Schedule I gives the payee's address as Milton, Wisconsin and the company's site lists Milton among its plants, while the record carries parent_hq_state IL, so the headquarters state is worth a second look even though the ownership answer does not change.

name: TOLEDO MOLDING AND DIE COMPANY
parent: GRAMMER AG (majority owned by Ningbo Jifeng Auto Parts Co., Ltd. of China through Jiye Auto Parts GmbH)
notes: Grant year FY2023 (July 2022-June 2023); acquisition October 2018, more than three years before the grant year began. Toledo Molding & Die's own website, in a capture archived October 17, 2021, says 'Since October 2018, TMD is part of GRAMMER Group' (http://web.archive.org/web/20211017153805/http://www.tmdinc.com/about-tmd/). GRAMMER AG's own history page lists '2018 Takeover of TMD Toledo Molding & Die Inc.' and GRAMMER AG's address is Grammer-Allee 2, 92289 Ursensollen, Germany. The same site records the 2018 takeover offer from Jiye Auto Parts GmbH, the vehicle through which Ningbo Jifeng Auto Parts of China took control of GRAMMER, so a strict ultimate-parent reading would put the top of the chain in China. The evidence here is company websites, not filings, so the grade is C. The 5000+ band is the weakest part: GRAMMER's own site says it has more than 42 production and distribution sites in 20 countries, but I could not fetch a page or report giving its worldwide headcount, so the band rests on that footprint rather than a published number. Grammer sold TMD in October 2024, after the grant year. This moves $40,000 out of the Ohio column.

name: SAF-HOLLAND INC

The group's worldwide headcount around 2020 was in the low thousands, which is the 500-4999 band the record already carries, so the only change is the headquarters, from Michigan to Germany. No Ohio dollars are involved. Grade C: this rests on company web pages read today rather than on a filing from the grant year.
